title: Deprecate legacy weight adapters; introduce hydration orchestrator
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Replace multiple legacy checkpoint adapters and ad-hoc shard loaders with a single hydration orchestrator that centralizes format negotiation, streaming checksum validation, and atomic shard activation. This ticket targets the operational complexity and latency variability when onboarding large model assets (>=50GB). Goals: reduce cold-load tail latency, simplify codepaths for model engineers, and provide a clear upgrade path from old weight adapters to a versioned manifest-driven onboarding flow.
acceptance_criteria: [1] New hydration orchestrator implements format negotiation API and passes all current loader unit/integration tests. [2] End-to-end model cold-start P50 <= 3.0s for 70B class models on dedicated test fleet (baseline 7.2s). [3] No regressions on serving correctness (generate identical outputs to before within established eval prompts). [4] Legacy adapters are feature-flagged off behind an opt-in shim; deprecation notice scheduled. [5] Migration doc + runbook published in Confluence.
tasks: Design hydration orchestrator contract and wire protocol (manifest v2) - design doc in Confluence
Implement negotiation layer: detect format, map to canonical reader, expose progressive streaming API
Add checksum streaming validator and fast-fail on corruption; integrate metrics (load_time, validation_time, bytes_streamed)
Implement atomic shard activation: two-phase commit for weights + tokenizer offset sanity check
Create compatibility shim that routes existing legacy adapters into orchestrator to validate behavior
Run performance benchmarks on dedicated QA fleet; iterate on concurrency/batching knobs
Roll out behind feature flag with canary traffic for 2 weeks; collect regressions and perf deltas
Deprecation plan: schedule removal of legacy adapters after migration window and customer notice
decisions: Use a manifest-driven approach (manifest v2) rather than probing heuristics — gives explicit format/metadata and simplifies downstream cache keys
Streaming checksum validation (rolling SHA256) preferred over full-file read for large shard files to avoid extra I/O stalls
Atomic activation will use ephemeral symlink semantics in object store mounts for deterministic rollbacks
Keep tokenizer initialization outside of the critical fast-path but verify offsets in the two-phase activation to prevent silent tokenization drift
tradeoffs: Manifest-driven onboarding increases upfront metadata management (maintainers must keep manifests accurate) but reduces runtime guessing and improves cache hits
Streaming validation slightly increases CPU during load but avoids repeated full reads and reduces error-handling complexity
Centralizing format negotiation reduces duplication but increases the size/complexity of a single component — mitigated by a small, well-separated plugin interface
risks: Regression in exact generation outputs if tokenizer offset sanity checks are incomplete
Undiscovered legacy formats used by a small set of internal customers could fail migration — we will run a discovery job against the model catalog
Performance regressions under high-concurrency cold-start traffic — mitigation: controlled canary and autoscaler guardrails
qa_plan: Unit tests for each format adapter shim, integration tests with model-serving stack using representative 7B/70B checkpoints, fuzz tests that corrupt a random byte to validate fast-fail paths, and a 2-week canary with rollout metrics (load latency, error rate, mem overhead).
metrics_targets: Migration success rate >= 99% for models in model-catalog tagged 'auto-migrate'
